authoredSolutions.1: For a particle of mass \(m\) with kinetic energy \(K\), \(p=\sqrt{2mK}\) so \[\lambda=\frac{h}{p}=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}.\] With the same energy for all three, \(\lambda\propto\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}\). Since \(m_{e}<m_{p}<m_{\alpha}\), the order of wavelengths reverses: \(\lambda_{\alpha}<\lambda_{p}<\lambda_{e}\). Hence the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.2: Let the total distance be \(2s\). The first half takes \(t_{1}=\frac{s}{6}\). The second half is covered in two equal intervals \(t\): \[9t+15t=24t=s\ \Rightarrow\ t=\frac{s}{24},\] so the second half takes \(2t=\frac{s}{12}\). Therefore \[v_{av}=\frac{2s}{\frac{s}{6}+\frac{s}{12}}=\frac{2s}{\frac{s}{4}}=8\ m/s.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.3: The amplitude of the magnetic field is \[B_{0}=\frac{E_{0}}{c}=\frac{60}{3\times 10^{8}}=2\times 10^{-7}\ T,\] which already eliminates the options carrying \(60\). The propagation constant is \[k=\frac{2\pi}{\lambda}=\frac{2\pi}{4\times 10^{-3}}=\frac{\pi}{2}\times 10^{3}\ m^{-1}.\] Since \(\vec{E}\) is along \(\hat{j}\) and propagation is along \(\hat{i}\), \(\vec{B}\) lies along \(\hat{k}\). Hence \(B_{z}=2\times 10^{-7}\sin\left[\frac{\pi}{2}\times 10^{3}\left(x-3\times 10^{8}t\right)\right]\hat{k}\ T\), and the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.4: For a diverging (concave) lens with a real object, \(f<0\) and \(u<0\), so \[\frac{1}{v}=\frac{1}{u}+\frac{1}{f}<0,\] i.e. \(v\) is negative and the image always lies on the same side as the object. It is therefore never formed on the other side of the lens, and Statement I is false. The same relation shows \(|v|<|u|\) with an erect, virtual, diminished image for every real object position, so Statement II is true. The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.5: The emitted photon energy equals the band gap, so \[\lambda=\frac{hc}{E_{g}}=\frac{1240\ eV\,nm}{1.42\ eV}\approx 873\ nm.\] The nearest printed value is \(875\ nm\), so the correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.6: The shell's mass uses only the solid material: \[W=\frac{4}{3}\pi\left(\frac{D^{3}-d^{3}}{8}\right)\sigma\rho_{w}g,\] while the buoyant force uses the full outer volume, \[F_{b}=\frac{4}{3}\pi\left(\frac{D^{3}}{8}\right)\rho_{w}g.\] For it to just float, \(W=F_{b}\), so \[\left(D^{3}-d^{3}\right)\sigma=D^{3}\ \Rightarrow\ 1-\frac{d^{3}}{D^{3}}=\frac{1}{\sigma}\ \Rightarrow\ \frac{d^{3}}{D^{3}}=\frac{\sigma-1}{\sigma}.\] Hence \(\frac{D}{d}=\left(\frac{\sigma}{\sigma-1}\right)^{1/3}\) and the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.7: The figure shows three steps whose facing areas are each \(\frac{A}{3}\) and whose separations from the flat plate are \(d\), \(2d\) and \(3d\). All three share the same pair of plates, so they are in parallel: \[C=\frac{\varepsilon_{0}A}{3d}+\frac{\varepsilon_{0}A}{3(2d)}+\frac{\varepsilon_{0}A}{3(3d)}=\frac{\varepsilon_{0}A}{3d}\left(1+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}\right)=\frac{\varepsilon_{0}A}{3d}\cdot\frac{11}{6}.\] Thus \(C=\frac{11\varepsilon_{0}A}{18d}\) and the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.8: For an Atwood machine, \[a=\left(\frac{m_{2}-m_{1}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\right)g=\frac{g}{8}.\] Hence \(8m_{2}-8m_{1}=m_{1}+m_{2}\), giving \(7m_{2}=9m_{1}\), i.e. \(\frac{m_{2}}{m_{1}}=\frac{9}{7}\). The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.9: Latent heat is heat per unit mass, \(L=\frac{Q}{m}\), so \[[L]=\frac{\left[ML^{2}T^{-2}\right]}{[M]}=\left[M^{0}L^{2}T^{-2}\right].\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.10: For an adiabatic change \(PV^{\gamma}\) is constant, so \[\frac{P_{i}}{P_{f}}=\left(\frac{V_{f}}{V_{i}}\right)^{\gamma}=\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{3/2}=\frac{4}{5}\sqrt{\frac{4}{5}}=\frac{4}{5}\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}=\frac{8}{5\sqrt{5}}.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.11: Using \(E=mc^{2}\) with \(m=1\ g=10^{-3}\ kg\), \[E=10^{-3}\times\left(3\times 10^{8}\right)^{2}=9\times 10^{13}\ J.\] Converting, \[E=\frac{9\times 10^{13}}{1.6\times 10^{-19}}\ eV=5.6\times 10^{32}\ eV=5.6\times 10^{26}\ MeV.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.12: With \(R_{e}=6370\ km\), the altitude \(h=318.5\ km=\frac{R_{e}}{20}\). On the surface (at rest) \[E_{i}=-\frac{GM_{e}m}{R_{e}},\] and in a circular orbit of radius \(R_{e}+h\), \[E_{f}=-\frac{GM_{e}m}{2\left(R_{e}+\frac{R_{e}}{20}\right)}=-\frac{10\,GM_{e}m}{21R_{e}}.\] Hence \[\Delta E=E_{f}-E_{i}=\frac{GM_{e}m}{R_{e}}\left(1-\frac{10}{21}\right)=\frac{11\,GM_{e}m}{21R_{e}},\] so \(x=11\) and the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.13: Statement I is true: for time varying currents the forces between two current elements are not equal and opposite, and momentum is conserved only when the momentum stored in the electromagnetic field is included, so Newton's third law survives only in that extended sense. Statement II is false: Ampere's circuital law is not independent of the Biot-Savart law; it can be derived from it for steady currents. Hence Statement I is true but Statement II is false, and the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.14: At \(x=0\), \(v=0\); at \(x=d\), \(v=\alpha\sqrt{d}\). By the work-energy theorem the total work done by all forces equals the change in kinetic energy: \[W=\frac{1}{2}m\left(\alpha\sqrt{d}\right)^{2}-0=\frac{m\alpha^{2}d}{2}.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.15: A shunt \(S\) is placed across the galvanometer so that at full scale \[i_{g}G=\left(i-i_{g}\right)S.\] With \(i_{g}=20\ \mu A\), \(G=200\ \Omega\) and \(i=20\ mA\), \[S=\frac{20\times 10^{-6}\times 200}{20\times 10^{-3}-20\times 10^{-6}}=\frac{4\times 10^{-3}}{1.998\times 10^{-2}}\approx 0.20\ \Omega.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.16: The bar's weight \(W\) acts at its midpoint. Taking torques about the point of contact with the ground, with \(L\) the length of the bar and \(R\) the force on the shoulder, \[W\left(\frac{L}{2}\cos\theta\right)=R\left(L\cos\theta\right)\ \Rightarrow\ R=\frac{W}{2}.\] The \(\cos\theta\) cancels, so the answer is independent of the inclination and the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.17: Given \(n\,MSD=(n+1)\,VSD\), one vernier division is \[1\,VSD=\frac{n}{n+1}MSD=\frac{nm}{n+1}.\] The least count is \[LC=1\,MSD-1\,VSD=m-\frac{nm}{n+1}=\frac{m}{n+1}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.18: Inserting a dielectric raises the capacitance \(C\), which lowers the capacitive reactance \(X_{C}=\frac{1}{\omega C}\). The series impedance \(Z=\sqrt{R^{2}+X_{C}^{2}}\) therefore falls, the current \(I=\frac{V}{Z}\) rises and the power \(I^{2}R\) dissipated in the bulb rises. The glow increases, so the correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.19: In the figure the vertical middle wire crosses the horizontal middle wire at a hop, so they are not joined. The plain wires therefore short the top-middle node to the bottom-middle node (call it \(P\)) and the middle-left node to the middle-right node (call it \(Q\)). Between \(P\) and \(Q\) there are exactly three paths: \[10+5=15\ \Omega,\qquad 11+4=15\ \Omega,\qquad 8+7=15\ \Omega,\] all in parallel, giving \(\frac{15}{3}=5\ \Omega\). Terminal \(A\) reaches \(P\) through \(6\ \Omega\) and terminal \(B\) reaches \(Q\) through \(8\ \Omega\), so \[R_{AB}=6+5+8=19\ \Omega.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.20: For an adiabatic process \(TV^{\gamma-1}\) is constant, so with \(\gamma=\frac{3}{2}\), \[TV^{1/2}=T_{f}(2V)^{1/2}\ \Rightarrow\ T_{f}=\frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}.\] The work done is \[W=\frac{nR\Delta T}{1-\gamma}=\frac{R\left(\frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}-T\right)}{-\frac{1}{2}}=2RT\left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)=RT\left(2-\sqrt{2}\right).\] The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.21: Squaring \(|\vec{a}+\vec{b}|=\sqrt{2}\,|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|\), \[a^{2}+b^{2}+2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=2\left(a^{2}+b^{2}-2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\right)\ \Rightarrow\ 6\,\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=a^{2}+b^{2}.\] With \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=ab\cos\theta=\frac{5}{9}ab\), \[\frac{10}{3}ab=a^{2}+b^{2}.\] Putting \(a=nb\) gives \(3n^{2}-10n+3=0\), so \(n=3\) or \(n=\frac{1}{3}\). The integer value is \(3\).
authoredSolutions.22: Every element of the half ring is the same distance \(R\) from the centre, so the potential simply adds as \[V=\frac{kQ}{R}=\frac{k(\lambda\pi R)}{R}=k\lambda\pi.\] With \(\lambda=4\ nC\,m^{-1}=4\times 10^{-9}\ C\,m^{-1}\), \[V=9\times 10^{9}\times 4\times 10^{-9}\pi=36\pi\ V.\] Hence \(x=36\). Note that the radius does not enter the answer.
authoredSolutions.23: The mass defect per triple-alpha reaction is \[\Delta m=3\times 4.0026-12=0.0078\ u,\] so \[Q=0.0078\times 931.5\approx 7.266\ MeV=7.266\times 10^{6}\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}=1.163\times 10^{-12}\ J.\] The number of such conversions per second follows from the power output, \[\frac{N}{t}=\frac{P}{Q}=\frac{5.808\times 10^{30}}{1.163\times 10^{-12}}\approx 5\times 10^{42}\ s^{-1}.\] Hence \(n=5\).
authoredSolutions.24: For two equal sources \(I=I_{max}\cos^{2}\left(\frac{\Delta\phi}{2}\right)\). Setting \(I=\frac{I_{max}}{4}\) gives \(\cos\left(\frac{\Delta\phi}{2}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\), so the smallest phase difference is \(\Delta\phi=\frac{2\pi}{3}\), i.e. a path difference of \(\frac{\lambda}{3}\). Then \[\frac{yd}{D}=\frac{\lambda}{3}\ \Rightarrow\ y=\frac{\lambda D}{3d}=\frac{600\times 10^{-9}\times 1}{3\times 1.0\times 10^{-3}}=2\times 10^{-4}\ m.\] Hence \(y=200\ \mu m\).
authoredSolutions.25: The pull acts tangentially at the rim, so \[\tau=FR=40\times 0.10=4\ N\,m,\qquad \alpha=\frac{\tau}{I}=\frac{4}{0.40}=10\ rad/s^{2}.\] Starting from rest, \[\omega=\alpha t=10\times 10=100\ rad/s,\] so \(x=100\).
authoredSolutions.26: The field depends only on \(x\), so the two sides parallel to the \(y\) axis sit in uniform but different fields while the forces on the other two sides cancel. Taking the loop from \(x=0\) to \(x=2\ m\), \[B(0)=B_{0}=5\ T,\qquad B(2)=B_{0}(1+8)=9B_{0}=45\ T.\] The two forces are opposite, so the net force is \[F=I\ell\left(9B_{0}-B_{0}\right)=8I\ell B_{0}=8\times 2\times 2\times 5=160\ N.\]
authoredSolutions.27: Two people pulling in opposite directions with \(200\ N\) each set up a tension of \(200\ N\) in the wire (not \(400\ N\)), exactly as a wall and one person would. Then \[\Delta\ell=\frac{F\ell}{AY}=\frac{200\times 2}{2\times 10^{-4}\times 1\times 10^{11}}=2\times 10^{-5}\ m=20\ \mu m.\]
authoredSolutions.28: On dc the inductor offers no reactance, so \[R=\frac{20}{5}=4\ \Omega.\] On ac the impedance is \[Z=\frac{20}{4}=5\ \Omega\ \Rightarrow\ X_{L}=\sqrt{Z^{2}-R^{2}}=\sqrt{25-16}=3\ \Omega.\] Hence \[L=\frac{X_{L}}{2\pi f}=\frac{3}{2\times 3\times 50}=0.01\ H=10\ mH.\]
authoredSolutions.30: The \(5\ V\) cell sits between \(B\) and \(D\), so take \(V_{D}=0\) and \(V_{B}=5\ V\). Let \(V_{A}=x\) and \(V_{C}=y\). Node \(A\) is joined to \(B\) and \(D\) by \(4\ \Omega\) each and to \(C\) by the \(10\ V\) cell in series with \(1\ \Omega\); node \(C\) is joined to \(B\) and \(D\) by \(2\ \Omega\) each. Kirchhoff's current law gives \[\frac{x-5}{4}+\frac{x-0}{4}+\frac{x-10-y}{1}=0\ \Rightarrow\ 6x-4y-45=0,\] \[\frac{y-5}{2}+\frac{y-0}{2}+\frac{y+10-x}{1}=0\ \Rightarrow\ 4y-2x+15=0.\] Adding, \(4x=30\), so \(x=7.5\ V\) and \(y=0\). The current in the \(1\ \Omega\) resistor is \[i=\frac{10+y-x}{1}=10-7.5=2.5\ A=\frac{25}{10}\ A,\] so \(n=25\).
authoredSolutions.61: \(L\) meets \(x-2=-y=z-1\) at \((2+t,-t,1+t)\) and \(2(x+1)=2(y-1)=z+1\) i.e. \(\frac{x+1}{1}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z+1}{2}\) at \((-1+s,1+s,-1+2s)\), with the joining vector \(\parallel(3,1,2)\). Solving \((s-t-3,s+t+1,2s-t-2)=k(3,1,2)\) gives \(t=-\tfrac43\), so \(L\) passes through \((\tfrac23,\tfrac43,-\tfrac13)\) with direction \((3,1,2)\). Setting \(x=-\tfrac13\) gives \(u=-\tfrac13\Rightarrow(y,z)=(1,-1)\).
authoredSolutions.62: Intersections of \(y^2=4x\) and \(x^2+y^2=5\): \(x^2+4x-5=0\Rightarrow x=1,\ y=\pm2\). Smaller area (right of parabola, inside circle) \(=2\int_0^2\big(\sqrt{5-y^2}-\tfrac{y^2}{4}\big)dy=2\big[1+\tfrac52\sin^{-1}\tfrac{2}{\sqrt5}-\tfrac23\big]=\frac{2}{3}+5\sin^{-1}\!\frac{2}{\sqrt5}\).
authoredSolutions.63: \((2y-5)dy=-3\,dx\Rightarrow y^2-5y=-3x+C\); through \((0,1)\): \(C=-4\), so \((y-\tfrac52)^2=-3(x-\tfrac34)\), a parabola with vertex \((\tfrac34,\tfrac52)\). Then \(2x+3y=\tfrac32+\tfrac{15}{2}=9\).
authoredSolutions.64: Reflect \(P(1,2)\) in the \(x\)-axis to \(P'(1,-2)\); line \(P'R\) (\(R(4,3)\)) meets \(x\)-axis at \(Q=(\tfrac{11}{5},0)\). For parallelogram \(PQRS\), midpoint of \(PR=\) midpoint of \(QS\): \((\tfrac52,\tfrac52)=\big(\tfrac{11/5+h}{2},\tfrac{k}{2}\big)\Rightarrow h=\tfrac{14}{5},\ k=5\). \(hk^2=\tfrac{14}{5}\cdot25=70\).
authoredSolutions.67: Write \(\frac{2\cos x-\sin x}{3\cos x+\sin x}=A(3\cos x+\sin x)+B(\cos x-3\sin x)\Rightarrow A=B=\tfrac12\). Thus \(\int=\tfrac12 x+\tfrac12\log|\sin x+3\cos x|+C\), giving \(\alpha=1,\ \beta=1,\ \gamma=3\), so \(\alpha+\tfrac{\gamma}{\beta}=4\).
authoredSolutions.68: Line \(\tfrac{x}{a}+\tfrac{y}{b}=1\) through \((3,5)\): \(\tfrac3a+\tfrac5b=1\ge2\sqrt{\tfrac{15}{ab}}\Rightarrow ab\ge60\). Minimum area \(=\tfrac12 ab=30\).
authoredSolutions.69: \(\cos\theta\cos(60^\circ-\theta)\cos(60^\circ+\theta)=\tfrac14\cos3\theta\); maximum of \(\cos3\theta\) under the bound is \(\tfrac12\), at \(3\theta\in\{\tfrac{\pi}{3},\tfrac{5\pi}{3},\tfrac{7\pi}{3},\tfrac{11\pi}{3},\tfrac{13\pi}{3},\tfrac{17\pi}{3}\}\), i.e. \(\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{9}(1,5,7,11,13,17)\). Sum \(=\tfrac{\pi}{9}\cdot54=6\pi\).
authoredSolutions.70: \(|\,2\vec a\times3\vec b\,|=6|\vec a\times\vec b|=15\Rightarrow|\vec a\times\vec b|=\tfrac52\). Quadrilateral \(OABC\) area \(=\tfrac12|\overrightarrow{OB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}|\); \(\overrightarrow{OB}=6\vec a+5\vec b,\ \overrightarrow{AC}=3\vec b-2\vec a\), cross \(=28(\vec a\times\vec b)\). Area \(=14\cdot\tfrac52=35\).
authoredSolutions.74: By Cramer + limit: \(x_c=\frac{c+1}{3c+2}\to\tfrac25=h\), \(y_c=\frac{-1}{5(3c+2)}\to-\tfrac1{25}=k\). Circle centre \((\tfrac25,-\tfrac1{25})\) through \((2,0)\): \(25x^2+25y^2-20x+2y-60=0\) (verified: \(100-40-60=0\)).
authoredSolutions.78: Area \(=\tfrac12|\vec a\times\vec b|=5\sqrt6\Rightarrow|\vec a\times\vec b|^2=600\). \(\vec a\times\vec b=(10,\,10-4\alpha,\,3\alpha-20)\Rightarrow25\alpha^2-200\alpha=0\Rightarrow\alpha=8\). \(\vec c=\vec a-\vec b=(3,1,-2)\Rightarrow|\vec c|^2=14\).
authoredSolutions.81: Real roots need \(b^2\ge4ac\) with \(a,b,c\in\{1,2,3,4\}\). Favourable counts: \(b=2{:}1,\ b=3{:}3,\ b=4{:}8\), total \(12\). Probability \(=\tfrac{12}{64}=\tfrac{3}{16}\Rightarrow m+n=19\).
authoredSolutions.83: \(f(x)=1+\lambda^2x-x^3\), local min at \(x=-\tfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt3}\). Numerator of the inequality is always positive, so need \((x+2)(x+3)<0\Rightarrow-3<-\tfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt3}<-2\Rightarrow2\sqrt3<\lambda<3\sqrt3\). \(\alpha^2+\beta^2=12+27=39\).
authoredSolutions.84: Each term \(=\tfrac1n\cdot\frac{1-r^2}{(1+r^2)\sqrt{1+r^4}}\) with \(r=k/n\), so limit \(=\int_0^1\frac{1-r^2}{(1+r^2)\sqrt{1+r^4}}dr\). Sub \(t=r+\tfrac1r\): \(=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\big[\tfrac{\pi}{2}-\sec^{-1}\sqrt2\big]=\tfrac{\pi}{4\sqrt2}=\tfrac{\pi}{\sqrt{32}}\). Thus \(k^2=32\).
authoredSolutions.86: As \(x\to\tfrac\pi2^-\), \(\frac{\tan8x}{\tan7x}\to0\), so left limit \(=(\tfrac87)^0=1=a-8\Rightarrow a=9\). Right limit \((1+|\cot x|)^{b/(a|\tan x|)}\)-type \(=e^{b/a}\) must equal \(1\Rightarrow b=0\). Hence \(a^2+b^2=81\).
authoredSolutions.88: Centre \((h,k)\) equidistant from \((0,0),(1,0)\Rightarrow h=\tfrac12\). Radius \(r=\sqrt{h^2+k^2}=\) distance to origin, and internal tangency to \(x^2+y^2=9\) gives \(r=3-r\Rightarrow r=\tfrac32\). So \(h^2+k^2=r^2=\tfrac94\), and \(4(h^2+k^2)=9\).
authoredSolutions.89: Cauchy on \(\mathbb{N}\) with \(f(1)=1\Rightarrow f(n)=n\). \(\sum_{k=1}^{2022}(\lambda+k)=2022\lambda+\tfrac{2022\cdot2023}{2}\le2022^2\Rightarrow\lambda\le\tfrac{2021}{2}=1010.5\). Largest natural \(\lambda=1010\).
authoredSolutions.91: The parent nucleus is at rest, so the total momentum stays zero: \[0=m_{1}v_{1}+m_{2}v_{2}\ \Rightarrow\ \vec{v}_{1}=-\frac{m_{2}}{m_{1}}\vec{v}_{2}.\] The fragments therefore fly apart in opposite directions and, with \(m_{1}:m_{2}=2:1\), their speeds are in the inverse ratio \(v_{1}:v_{2}=1:2\). The correct choice is A.
authoredSolutions.92: The figure shows a beam parallel to the axis entering \(L_{1}\) and leaving \(L_{2}\) parallel to the axis again. A parallel beam converges to the focus of \(L_{1}\), and to emerge parallel from \(L_{2}\) the rays must diverge from the focus of \(L_{2}\). The two foci therefore coincide, so the separation is \[d=f_{1}+f_{2}=10+15=25\ cm.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.93: The average translational kinetic energy is \(\frac{3}{2}k_{B}T\), so it is proportional to the absolute temperature. Here \[T_{i}=273-78=195\ K,\] and doubling the energy doubles the absolute temperature: \[T_{f}=390\ K=390-273=117\ ^{\circ}C.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.94: The \(n=1\rightarrow n=2\) gap in hydrogen is \[E_{2}-E_{1}=-3.4-(-13.6)=10.2\ eV,\] exactly the energy supplied, so the atom reaches only the first excited state. The single available downward transition \(2\rightarrow 1\) gives one spectral line. The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.95: The amplitudes are related by \(E_{0}=cB_{0}\), so \[E_{0}=3\times 10^{8}\times 3.5\times 10^{-7}=105\ V\,m^{-1},\] which rules out the options with \(1.17\) and \(10.5\). The wave travels along \(-\hat{i}\) (the phase is \(kx+\omega t\)) and \(\vec{B}\) is along \(\hat{j}\); since \(\vec{E}\times\vec{B}\) must point along the propagation direction and \(\hat{k}\times\hat{j}=-\hat{i}\), the electric field lies along \(\hat{k}\). Hence \(E_{z}=105\sin\left(1.5\times 10^{3}x+0.5\times 10^{11}t\right)V\,m^{-1}\) and the correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.96: At \(t=10\ s\) the loop has advanced \(2\times 10=20\ cm\), so its leading edge is \(20\ cm\) inside the \(50\ cm\) wide field region and its trailing edge is \(20-15=5\ cm\) inside. The whole loop lies within the field, so the flux \(\phi=BA\) is constant and \[e=-\frac{d\phi}{dt}=0.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.97: Each car stops after \[s=\frac{u^{2}}{2a}=\frac{20^{2}}{2\times 2}=100\ m,\] so together they close \(200\ m\). The remaining gap is \[300-200=100\ m.\] The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.98: The graph shows ordinary forward conduction in the first quadrant, but in the third quadrant the reverse current stays negligible until a sharp knee, beyond which it rises almost vertically at essentially constant voltage. That sharp reverse breakdown at a fixed voltage is the signature of a Zener diode, which is used as a voltage regulator. The correct choice is C.
authoredSolutions.99: For a soap bubble the excess pressure is \(\Delta P=\frac{4T}{r}\). Given \(\Delta P_{1}=3\Delta P_{2}\), \[\frac{4T}{r_{1}}=3\cdot\frac{4T}{r_{2}}\ \Rightarrow\ r_{2}=3r_{1}.\] Hence \[\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}=\left(\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}\right)^{3}=\frac{1}{27}.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.100: From \(\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}\), \[[h]=[\lambda]\sqrt{[m][E]}=L\sqrt{M\cdot ML^{2}T^{-2}}=L\cdot ML T^{-1}=\left[ML^{2}T^{-1}\right].\] The same follows from \(E=h\nu\). The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.101: For a circular orbit of radius \(r\), \(E=-\frac{GMm}{2r}\), and with \(GM=gR^{2}\), \[E_{i}=-\frac{gR^{2}m}{2(2R)}=-\frac{mgR}{4}=-\frac{10^{3}\times 10\times R}{4}=-2500R.\] After adding \(\frac{10^{4}R}{6}\), \[E_{f}=-2500R+\frac{10^{4}R}{6}=-\frac{2500R}{3}.\] Setting \(E_{f}=-\frac{gR^{2}m}{2r}=-\frac{10^{4}R^{2}}{2r}\), \[\frac{10^{4}R^{2}}{2r}=\frac{2500R}{3}\ \Rightarrow\ r=6R.\] The correct choice is D.
authoredSolutions.102: Between the left vertex \(L\) and the right vertex \(N\) there are three symmetric branches, each of two resistors: through the top vertex, through the centre and through the bottom vertex. By the left-right symmetry the midpoint of every branch sits at the same potential \(\frac{V_{L}+V_{N}}{2}\), so the two vertical resistors joining those midpoints carry no current and can be removed. The three branches of \(2R\) each then give \[R_{LN}=\frac{2R}{3}.\] Adding the two series resistors at the terminals, \[R_{AB}=R+\frac{2R}{3}+R=\frac{8R}{3}.\] The correct choice is B.
authoredSolutions.103: Gauss's law counts only the charge enclosed by \(S\). From the figure the charges inside are \(+5q\), \(+q\) and \(-2q\), while \(-4q\) and \(+3q\) lie outside.
